chunks: Three - Ali ibn Ahmad al-Bandaneeji narrated from Ubaydillah ibn Musa al-Alawi al-Abbasī, from al-Hasan ibn Mu'awiya, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbūb, from 'Isa ibn Sulayman, from al-Mufaddal ibn Umar, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) mentioning al-Qa'im (peace be upon him). I said: 'I hope that his matter will be easy.' He said: 'It will not be so until you wipe blood and sweat together.'

key_terms.أَمْرُهُ: His matter/affair (referring to the rise or event)
key_terms.الْعَلَق: Blood (specifically clotting blood or fresh blood)
key_terms.الْقَائِم: The Rising One (al-Qa'im), a title for the Twelfth Imam

ai.seo_question: What condition did Imam al-Sadiq set for the ease of al-Qa'im's rise?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Kitab al-Ghayba*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) corrects Al-Mufaddal ibn Umar’s optimism regarding the ease of the Mahdi’s rise, emphasizing that the transition to global justice requires a period of intense exertion. The phrase 'wiping blood and sweat' (imḥā’ al-‘alaq wa al-‘araq) symbolizes the arduous struggle and sacrifice of the believers during the pre-appearance distresses, a concept central to Shia eschatology as the necessary precursor to the establishment of divine rule.
